text: Review-only task for the native openvela factory demo board qualification. Read tools/board-tests/korvo_pair_transaction.py and related console/flash helpers, backups/cache-writeback-execution/run_services_v3.py, current factory profile/manifest/rcS and FactoryBackend interface. Produce a concrete bounded first-board-test plan and a PRIVATE runner candidate under this task directory ONLY. Do not access any serial/USB device, do not flash, do not execute board commands, do not modify maintained source, do not build firmware. Root owns hardware and integration. The firmware is FLAT, 16MiB Flash, kernel at 0x2000 up to before data 0xe00000, HMI LittleFS at 0xe00000 size 0x100000, original full backup via existing checkpoint. Preserve/restore original full flash checksum using paired transaction helper; do not use sd.compose with 2MiB assumption. Factory app org.openvela.s31.factorydemo/FactoryActivity exec s31factory, native SystemServerLite. Root adding intent actions s31.factory.snapshot/storage/record/stop/play/reset-audio/coffee/dashboard/close/led0..led3 through am start -n package/Activity -a action. Numeric snapshot lines will carry camera/captured/presented/audio/bytes/storage/probe/usb/led, asynchronous success requires fresh snapshot. Need verify boot/services/package registration, real camera progress, SD unique write/read/delete, open/close/reopen, coffee page resource loading, reboot. Listening and human input optional separate, no network tests, do not invent success. First run should bound each action, retain logs, always restore original firmware. Read actual APIs before constructing calls. Deliver result.md and candidate runner, no execution. Keep limited scope and finish promptly.

I’ll inspect the requested test/helper scripts and factory configuration, then write a bounded first-board-test plan plus a non-executed private runner candidate in the task directory. I’ll keep all work review-only and avoid device, flash, build, and maintained-source changes.

The board-evidence skill is relevant because this is a qualification/evidence-preservation review, so I’m checking its local procedure before drafting the plan. I will apply only its review and preservation guidance; no board operation is authorized here.

The paired transaction helper can cover the FLAT image and HMI data restore, but the older service runner’s image layout and console framing cannot be copied directly. I’m adapting the candidate to the 0x2000/0xe00000 layout and making asynchronous checks depend on fresh numeric snapshots rather than intent dispatch success.

Two concrete integration issues surfaced: the current shell line limit is 80 bytes, so several full intent commands need a checked component variable; and the current `am` parser does not support `-n`. I’ll mark `-n` support as a preflight blocker and keep the candidate fail-closed. The snapshot and backend code now provide usable camera, SD, audio, LED, and coffee completion checks.

The private draft now includes one bounded sequence, reopen and reboot checks, and restoration of the full range from 0x2000 onward followed by a checksum comparison of all 16 MiB. I’m reviewing the draft’s failure paths and evidence claims. It has no live CLI, and I have only parsed its syntax—not imported or run it.

Delivered privately in the task directory:

- [result.md](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/board-runner-review/result.md): bounded test plan, acceptance criteria and restoration requirements.
- [runner_candidate.py](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/board-runner-review/runner_candidate.py): unexecuted candidate using paired restoration and fresh snapshots.

Critical blocker: current `am` accepts `-t`, not `-n`, and rejects unknown options with exit status 0. The candidate blocks preparation until Root resolves this.
